title: Existing customer — order status + damaged item

mistakes.customer_said: Okay, thank you — what does that actually mean for me, will someone call or email me? And will I be getting a replacement cushion or a refund?
mistakes.ema_said: I'll get this escalated for you right now.
mistakes.problem: Ema said she would escalate but never filed a support ticket (no ticket reference given) and never asked for a real email to file one with. Instead she deflected the customer to email support themselves.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The spec says she can file a ticket with just a real email and a description — no order verification needed. The customer was left to do the work and no record exists.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Ask for a working email and call submit_support_ticket, then give the ticket reference.

mistakes.customer_said: Okay, thank you — what does that actually mean for me, will someone call or email me? And will I be getting a replacement cushion or a refund?
mistakes.ema_said: Your torn cushion is covered under our 5-year Comfort & Craftsmanship Warranty for cushion retention, so a replacement cushion or component is the typical fix rather than a refund.
mistakes.problem: A specifically-named '5-year Comfort & Craftsmanship Warranty' with 'cushion retention' coverage is stated as fact; this appears fabricated and is not supported by anything shown as verified policy.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Inventing warranty terms creates a false expectation and potential liability if the real policy differs.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Quote warranty terms only from get_shop_policies('warranty').

mistakes.customer_said: Okay, thank you — what does that actually mean for me, will someone call or email me? And will I be getting a replacement cushion or a refund?
mistakes.ema_said: They'll review it and get back to you within 48 hours with instructions for the replacement.
mistakes.problem: A 48-hour response SLA is asserted without any verified policy source, and repeated again as confirmation.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Sets a concrete commitment the company may not meet, eroding trust on an already-negative experience.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Only state response times documented in the contact/support policy.

mistakes.customer_said: That's the email I have on my confirmation, so I'm not sure what else to give you.
mistakes.ema_said: the fastest next step is to email our support team directly at tempestfurniture@gmail.com
mistakes.problem: A support email address is provided that was not verified via get_shop_policies('contact'); it appears invented.
mistakes.why_it_matters: If the address is wrong, the customer's damage claim goes nowhere.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Pull the real support contact from the policies tool.

mistakes.customer_said: Sure, the order number is 1001, and the email is priya.wrong@gmail.com.
mistakes.ema_said: Let me check that for you.
mistakes.problem: Filler 'let me check' announcement is explicitly banned by the spec; she should look up silently and answer once.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Reads/sounds robotic and stalls the call.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Remove filler; give the lookup result in one natural message.

mistakes.customer_said: It's priya.nair@example.com — that's the one I used.
mistakes.problem: Terse, unempathetic reply with no explanation or next step offered to a customer with a damaged product.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Feels dismissive during a support escalation where empathy is required.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Explain the mismatch warmly and immediately offer the ticket path.

mistakes.customer_said: Are you sure? That's definitely the email I used, and the order number is 1001 — can you try searching by my name, Priya Nair?
mistakes.ema_said: "priya.nair@example.com" is a placeholder domain, not a real one, so the system can't use it.
mistakes.problem: Ema asserts a technical reason for the failure (placeholder domain rejected by the system) that she cannot know; the tool simply failed to match.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Speculating about system internals and effectively accusing the customer of giving a fake email damages trust and may be wrong.
mistakes.suggested_fix: Say the order/email combination didn't match and offer the ticket route instead of theorizing.
